land.text: the Danish and Norwegian realms of the Kalmar Union (Cliopatria: 2,947 of the 2,948 cells of the 1526 shape lie in the 1525 Kalmar Union shape)

predecessors.note: Sweden left the Kalmar Union with Gustav Vasa's election on 6 June 1523 (Denmark-Norway page); Cliopatria's Kalmar Union row ends in 1525 and this row starts in 1526.

successors.note: The Danish kingdom after the Treaty of Kiel of 14 January 1814: Denmark, Schleswig and Holstein, Iceland and the Faroe Islands. Split from the same Cliopatria row (shapes 1814-1940).

land.text: the Kingdom of Norway, ceded to the King of Sweden by Article IV of the Treaty of Kiel; Norway declared independence on 17 May 1814 and the union with Sweden was 'formally established when the Storting elected Charles XIII as king of Norway on 4 November 1814'

successors.note: Cliopatria's Kingdom of Norway row (1814-2024) holds Norway in 1814 (shape kingdom-of-norway_1814, 346,290 km2); the union with Sweden followed on 4 November 1814 and Cliopatria's Sweden-Norway row starts in 1815. Corrected by the eu-14-g reviewer: the earlier note said Norway had no shape in 1814.

capitals.name: Copenhagen (København)
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Capital: Copenhagen'; the page gives no capital years, so the span is the state's life.

rulers.name: Frederick I
rulers.note: 13 April 1523 to 10 April 1533; the state is drawn from 1526. The page lists no interregnum 1533-1534.

rulers.name: Christian III
rulers.note: 4 July 1534 to 1 January 1559. The Denmark-Norway page's infobox counts his reign as 1537-1559.

rulers.name: Christian VII
rulers.note: 14 January 1766 to 13 March 1808; Frederick VI ruled as regent and de facto king from 14 April 1784 (Denmark-Norway page footnote).

rulers.name: Frederick VI
rulers.note: 13 March 1808; king of Denmark until 3 December 1839, of Norway until the Treaty of Kiel.

correction.text: shape unchanged; years only: it holds 1526-1559, the Livonian purchase of 1559 and Magnus's landing of 1560 come in the next keyframe

keyframe_review.note: Holds 1526-1559; 1560-1563 are covered by the new keyframe denmark-norway_1560. 612,437 km2 (2,948 cells): Denmark, Norway with Jämtland, Härjedalen and Idre-Särna, Iceland and the Faroes. Size check: the page's 1800 infobox gives 2,655,567 km2, of which Greenland is 2,166,086 km2; without Greenland that is 489,481 km2 against Cliopatria's 526,384 km2 for 1775-1806 (ratio 1.08, fine). Greenland is not in this row's shapes (no cell west of Iceland's -24.4 W); Cliopatria draws the colony as its own row, Greenland (1734-1940); see notes. The page dates the dual monarchy to 1537, so 1526-1536 is the Danish realm after the Kalmar Union, kept for continuity.

union.text: the Bishopric of Ösel-Wiek and Courland's Pilten, bought by Frederick II (Ösel itself is Saare)
the island of Ösel (Saaremaa)

correction.text: the 1526 shape plus the Bishopric of Ösel-Wiek and Courland's Pilten and the island of Ösel, bought in 1559 and taken up by Magnus in 1560

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's first Danish Livonia is the 1564 shape, but the Magnus page has Frederick II buy Ösel-Wiek and Courland in 1559 ('sold his lands to King Frederick II for 30,000 thalers') and Magnus land on Ösel in 1560; the Denmark-Norway page has Frederick II 'purchased the island of Osel in 1560'. The cells are those Cliopatria draws in 1564-1571 (36 mainland cells in Estonia and Latvia plus Ösel).

Holds 1564-1569. Jämtland, Härjedalen and Idre-Särna (about 330 cells, 10 of them in Västerbotten) are out because Sweden 're-occupied Jemtland, as well as Herjedalen and Trøndelag' in 1564 and returned them in 1570; the Estonia-Latvia cells are Magnus's lands; the 3 Västra Götaland cells are Älvsborg, taken by Denmark ('captured Sweden's gateway to the west, Älvsborg Fortress, after only three days of bombardment'). Cliopatria ends the occupation in 1571, the page in 1570: see denmark-norway_1570. Occupied Jämtland and the Älvsborg front are the contest zone in the ledger.

correction.text: the 1564 shape with Jämtland, Härjedalen and Idre-Särna (and the rest of Ösel) back in Danish-Norwegian hands

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1570-1571: Jämtland and Härjedalen 'were later regained by Denmark-Norway following the peace process in 1570' ('returned to Denmark-Norway in 1570'), a year before Cliopatria's 1572 shape. Magnus's Livonian lands are still in the Danish sphere until Cliopatria's 1572 (page silent).

1572-1594: Norway with Jämtland and Härjedalen, all of Ösel, no Livonian mainland, no Älvsborg. The Stettin terms on the page: 'The Swedes ransomed Älvsborg with 150,000 riksdaler'; the loss of Magnus's Wiek and Pilten has no dated sentence on the Magnus page, so the 1572 date is Cliopatria's (ledger confidence 1).

1595-1611: 24 cells of East Finnmark (69.1-70.2 N, 26.1-30.6 E) are added. Unverified: page budget; none of the pages opened dates a Finnmark frontier in 1595. The Kalmar War page says only that the 1613 peace brought 'incorporating Lapland as a part of Norway'.

1612-1618: differs from the previous shape by 4 cells on the Swedish frontier (Västra Götaland, Värmland, Vestfold, Finnmark), which no page explains. The Kalmar War is not in the shape: Kalmar was returned at Knäred and Älvsborg was only held in pledge, so both are ledger events, not territory.
1619-1621: the 4-cell swap of 1612 reverses; area back to 620,907 km2. The end of the Älvsborg pledge is dated 1619 only by Cliopatria (ledger confidence 1).
1622-1625: 5 cells on the lower Elbe (Hamburg 3, Niedersachsen 1, Schleswig-Holstein 1) added. Unverified: page budget; the Lübeck page does not mention them.

correction.text: the 1622 shape: Danish-Norwegian territory without the Lower Saxon theatre, which is a contest zone 1625-1629 (ledger); Holstein and Jutland are contested from September 1627

keyframe_review.note: 1626-1628: 55 cells of the Lower Saxon theatre (51.6-53.5 N, 9.3-12.4 E) are added, to 634,295 km2, the largest Danish-Norwegian shape. The page calls these 'claims to Lower Saxon bishoprics' that Christian IV was 'obliged' to cede in 1629 and says the Danish armies' initial success of 1625 turned in 1626 at Dessau Bridge and Lutter am Barenberge, so the zone is contested ground, not Danish territory. The same shape draws Holstein and Jutland as Danish while Wallenstein and Tilly 'invaded Danish Holstein in September' 1627 and advanced through Jutland; both are contest events.

correction.text: the pre-war possessions 'restored to Christian' by the Treaty of Lübeck: the 1632 shape (Denmark, Holstein, Norway with Jämtland, Iceland, Faroes, Halland, Gotland, Ösel)

keyframe_review.note: 1629-1631: Cliopatria removes 127 cells (Schleswig-Holstein 58, Syddanmark 7, Lower Saxony 38, Saxony-Anhalt 16, ...) and gives 107 of them to its Habsburg Monarchy row. The Treaty of Lübeck of 22 May 1629 'restored to Christian his pre-war possessions' and the page names no later Habsburg hold on Holstein or Jutland, so Holstein, Schleswig and Jutland stay Danish-Norwegian; the Lower Saxon cells are the renounced claims. Use the 1632 shape.

1632-1644: 620,907 km2, the shape the Brömsebro page's cession list implies: Jämtland and Härjedalen (and Idre-Särna), Gotland, Ösel and Halland are all in it. The Bremen-Verden prince-bishoprics, under a Danish administrator from 1635, are not drawn ('transferred from Danish to Swedish control' in 1645 on the Brömsebro page).

Holds 1645-1657 (Cliopatria runs it to 1658; the Treaty of Roskilde is of February 1658). Out: Jämtland, Härjedalen, Idre-Särna, Gotland, Ösel and Halland (391 cells). 10 Västerbotten cells leave with Jämtland, which no page opened names. Halland was only a 30-year guarantee in 1645 but 'was now permanently ceded' in 1658, so it is drawn Swedish throughout.

correction.text: the 1659 shape without the Gottorp part of Schleswig: the Treaty of Roskilde (1658) 'recognized the sovereignty of its dukes over the Gottorp portions of the duchy of Schleswig'

keyframe_review.note: Holds 1658-1659. Out: Scania, Blekinge, Bohuslän, Trøndelag and Bornholm ('the ceded lands comprising Blekinge, Bornholm, Bohuslän, Scania and Trøndelag, as well as Halland'): 423 cells, 551,111 km2 falling to 471,810 km2. Two cautions: Cliopatria also removes 46 cells of Møre og Romsdal, which the page places in the ceded Trøndelag ('Trøndelag then included Nordmøre and Romsdal'), and 8 of Kronoberg which the page does not name (unverified), and the 1659 shape still contains the ducal Schleswig that the Gottorp dukes held in sovereignty from 1658, so the correction removes it (34 cells).

correction.text: Denmark-Norway after the Treaty of Copenhagen: Trøndelag and Bornholm restored, the Gottorp part of Schleswig ducal

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1660-1661: 'the resulting Treaty of Copenhagen in 1660 restored Trøndelag to Norway, and the island of Bornholm to Denmark' (Denmark-Norway page: 'which gave Trøndelag and Bornholm back'); Scania, Blekinge, Bohuslän and Halland 'remained Swedish'. Cliopatria shows the return only in 1662.

1662-1669: the shape after the return of Trøndelag and Bornholm and without the Gottorp part of Schleswig (the dukes' sovereignty under the Treaties of Roskilde and Copenhagen, Holstein-Gottorp page). The Cliopatria Holy Roman Empire Minor States row carries those cells until 1712; the eu-09 notes already doubt that.

1670-1708: +15 cells in Lower Saxony, the County of Oldenburg and Delmenhorst: 'Danish kings ruled the county, in a personal union from 1667-1773' (page). Cliopatria starts it three years after the 1667 inheritance date on the page.
1709-1712: the 1670 shape unchanged; 'Denmark rejoined the war in 1709 in a campaign to regain their lost provinces' (Scania), which moved no border.

correction.text: the 1709 shape; Bremen-Verden and the ducal Schleswig are occupations (ledger) until 1715 and 1720

keyframe_review.note: 1713-1717 adds Bremen-Verden (27 cells) and the Gottorp part of Schleswig (33 cells) to the 1709 shape. Bremen-Verden was a Danish occupation of 1712-1715 ('Denmark-Norway occupied plague stricken Bremen-Verden' in 1712; 'sold to him Bremen-Verden, which it kept under occupation since 1712' in 1715), and the ducal Schleswig was occupied by Danish troops until the Treaty of Frederiksborg gave Denmark 'full control over Schleswig' in 1720. Occupied land is not territory, so the territory is the 1709 shape; the occupations are ledger events.

correction.text: the 1709 shape for 1718-July 1720 (occupations in the ledger); the 1721 shape from 3 July 1720

keyframe_review.note: 1718-1720: as the 1713 shape (Bremen-Verden went to Hanover in 1715, but Cliopatria keeps its 27 cells until 1721); the ducal Schleswig is still an occupation until 3 July 1720, when 'Denmark also gained full control over Schleswig', and from then the territory is the 1721 shape.

1721-1743: 529,212 km2: the 1709 shape plus the whole of Schleswig (the Treaty of Frederiksborg, 3 July 1720: 'Denmark also gained full control over Schleswig'). The page also has 'Danish-held areas of Swedish Pomerania were returned to Sweden', which Cliopatria never drew.
1744-1774: the same 2,498 cells as 1721; stable between the Treaty of Frederiksborg and the exchange of 1773.

1775-1806: 15 Oldenburg cells out, 5 ducal Holstein cells in: the Treaty of Tsarskoye Selo of 1773, by which the Gottorp side 'obtained the German countships of Oldenburg and Delmenhorst' (Holstein-Gottorp page; 'in a personal union from 1667-1773' on the Denmark-Norway page). Cliopatria draws it two years late.
1807-1808: 3 cells fewer (Hamburg, Niedersachsen, Syddanmark), which Cliopatria gives to its First French Empire row. Unverified: page budget.
1809-1813: Norway, Denmark, Schleswig and Holstein, Iceland and the Faroes, 526,207 km2, until the Treaty of Kiel; one more Finnmark cell goes to the Russian Empire in 1809 (unverified: page budget).

region.text: Denmark and Norway (with Jämtland and Härjedalen), Iceland and the Faroes under the Danish crown, as Cliopatria draws them from 1526

ledger.note: 1526: Denmark and Norway stand as one realm under the Danish crown after Sweden left the Kalmar Union. Cliopatria's first shape is 1526, a year after its Kalmar Union row ends; the page says 'Following Sweden's departure in 1523, the union was effectively dissolved' and dates the dual monarchy 1537-1814, and is silent on 1526.

1537: the Norwegian riksråd is abolished and Norway is bound to Denmark in a dual monarchy. Infobox 'Dual monarchy (Real union) (1537-1814)', 'Norwegian riksråd abolished: 1537', 'in 1537 he also secured Norway, creating the union between the two kingdoms'. Nothing changes hands; the colour continues.

region.text: the Bishopric of Ösel-Wiek and Courland's Pilten, bought by Frederick II (Ösel itself is Saare)

ledger.note: 1559: Frederick II buys the Bishopric of Ösel-Wiek and Courland. 'Johannes V von Münchhausen, prince-bishop of Ösel-Wiek and Courland, sold his lands to King Frederick II for 30,000 thalers'; Frederick II 'gave that territory to his younger brother Magnus', who landed on Ösel in 1560 (Denmark-Norway page: Frederick II 'purchased the island of Osel in 1560'). The region is the Estonian and Latvian cells Cliopatria draws in 1564-1571, with Ösel itself in the 1560 keyframe.

region.text: the Swedish-Norwegian marches (Jemtland, Herjedalen, Trøndelag) and the Älvsborg-Båhus front on the Göta älv

ledger.note: 1563: war with Sweden. 'On 13 August 1563, war was declared by emissaries from Denmark and Lübeck in Stockholm'; Sweden 'occupied the undefended Norwegian province of Jemtland' (retaken, then 're-occupied in 1564' with Härjedalen and an attempt on Trøndelag, 'repelled'), Denmark took Älvsborg, and Sweden held Båhus Fortress 'but lost it in 1566'. The page gives the year of the war, not of each campaign.

union.text: the Norwegian provinces of Jemtland and Herjedalen

Älvsborg and Gullberg, 'both in present-day Gothenburg'

region.text: the Swedish-Norwegian marches and the Älvsborg-Båhus front

ledger.note: 13 December 1570: the Treaty of Stettin ends the war, 'Status quo ante bellum in Scandinavia'. Jämtland and Härjedalen are 'returned to Denmark-Norway in 1570'; 'The Swedes ransomed Älvsborg with 150,000 riksdaler'; 'The Swedish king withdrew the claims to Norway, Skåne, Halland, Blekinge, and Gotland'.

region.text: Magnus's mainland lands (Wiek and Courland's Pilten) as Cliopatria draws them 1564-1571

ledger.note: 1572: Magnus's mainland lands in Estonia (Wiek, Pärnu, Rapla) pass to Russia in Cliopatria's draw. Page silent on the date: Magnus was 'titular King of Livonia from 1570 to 1578' as a vassal of Ivan IV and had abandoned the siege of Reval by the end of March 1571; the Danish crown kept Ösel.

region.text: Magnus's mainland lands (Wiek and Courland's Pilten) as Cliopatria draws them 1564-1571

ledger.note: 1572: Courland's Pilten (Ventspils, Dundaga, Kuldiga) passes to Poland-Lithuania in Cliopatria's draw. Page silent on the date; Magnus spent his last six years at Pilten as a pensioner of the Polish crown (died 1583).

region.text: East Finnmark (Varanger and the Pasvik valley), 24 cells at 69.1-70.2 N, 26.1-30.6 E

ledger.note: 1595: Cliopatria extends Finnmark east to the Pasvik. Page silent: none of the pages opened dates this frontier; the Kalmar War page says only that the peace of 1613 meant 'incorporating Lapland as a part of Norway'. Unverified: page budget.

union.text: the city and castle of Kalmar
Älvsborg and Gullberg, 'both in present-day Gothenburg'

region.text: Kalmar and the Älvsborg-Gullberg fortresses near Gothenburg

ledger.note: 1611: Denmark-Norway attacks Sweden. 'Denmark-Norway declared war upon Sweden and invaded' in April 1611; 'A Danish force of 5,200 laid siege to the city of Kalmar, ultimately taking it' (no date on the page) and Älvsborg and Gullberg were taken in early 1612 (page). Counterpart slug: Cliopatria's Swedish Empire row starts in 1612, the Kingdom of Sweden row has no neighbour of this state after 1611.

union.text: the city and castle of Kalmar
Älvsborg and Gullberg, 'both in present-day Gothenburg'

region.text: Kalmar and the Älvsborg-Gullberg fortresses near Gothenburg

ledger.note: 20 January 1613: the Treaty of Knäred. 'All conquests made by both sides are returned' (infobox), so Kalmar goes back to Sweden; 'Sweden pays 1 million rixdollars as ransom for Älvsborg' and 'Swedish ships are allowed free passage through The Sound'. The page also has Denmark-Norway 'incorporating Lapland as a part of Norway' without a boundary; not drawn.

region.text: Älvsborg and Gullberg, 'both in present-day Gothenburg'

ledger.note: January 1613: Denmark holds Älvsborg and Gullberg until the ransom is paid (infobox 'Älvsborg temporarily controlled by Denmark (1613)'). Page silent on how long.

region.text: Älvsborg and Gullberg, 'both in present-day Gothenburg'

ledger.note: 1619: the Älvsborg pledge ends. Page silent: the Kalmar War page gives no date for the payment of the ransom; the year is that of the 4-cell change in Cliopatria's 1619 shape.

region.text: 5 cells on the lower Elbe (53.5-53.7 N, 9.4-10.3 E)

ledger.note: 1622: Cliopatria adds 5 cells on the lower Elbe (Hamburg 3, Niedersachsen 1, Schleswig-Holstein 1). Page silent; unverified: page budget.

region.text: the Lower Saxon theatre of 1625-1626 (the 'Lower Saxon bishoprics' of the page) between the Weser and the Elbe-Saale, 51.6-53.5 N, 9.3-12.4 E

ledger.note: 1625: Christian IV enters the Thirty Years' War in Lower Saxony. 'The war, known in Danish as Kejserkrigen, began in 1625. Initial success was with the Danish armies'; the tide turned in 1626 at Dessau Bridge and Lutter am Barenberge. The zone is the 55 cells Cliopatria adds in 1626.

region.text: Danish Holstein and Jutland as far as the Limfjord

ledger.note: September 1627: the Imperial armies invade Danish land. 'In 1627, Wallenstein and Tilly joined forces and invaded Danish Holstein in September before advancing through Jutland as far as the Limfjord'. Held by Imperial troops without annexation until the peace.

region.text: the Lower Saxon theatre of 1625-1626 (the 'Lower Saxon bishoprics' of the page) between the Weser and the Elbe-Saale, 51.6-53.5 N, 9.3-12.4 E

ledger.note: 22 May 1629: the Treaty of Lübeck. Christian IV 'was obliged to cede his claims to Lower Saxon bishoprics', stay out of imperial affairs and end his North German alliances; the zone stays with the Empire's side.

region.text: Danish Holstein and Jutland as far as the Limfjord

ledger.note: 22 May 1629: 'The treaty restored to Christian his pre-war possessions'; Holstein and Jutland are Danish again. Cliopatria instead gives Holstein to its Habsburg Monarchy row until 1631; see the keyframe verdict on denmark-norway_1629.

union.text: the Norwegian provinces of Jemtland and Herjedalen
Idre and Särna

region.text: the Norwegian provinces of Jemtland and Herjedalen, with Idre and Särna

ledger.note: 13 August 1645: the Treaty of Brömsebro ends the Torstenson War. 'Denmark-Norway ceded the Norwegian provinces of Jämtland and Härjedalen'; of Idre and Särna 'The concession of this region was not formally recognised until 1751'.

union.text: the island of Ösel (Saaremaa)

region.text: 'the Danish Baltic Sea islands of Gotland and Saaremaa'

ledger.note: 13 August 1645: Gotland and Ösel go to Sweden at Brömsebro. Frederick II had 'purchased the island of Osel in 1560' (Denmark-Norway page).

region.text: the Danish province of Halland

ledger.note: 13 August 1645: 'Sweden received the Danish province of Halland for a period of 30 years as a guarantee'. Drawn Swedish from 1645 like Cliopatria; the Roskilde page says it 'was now permanently ceded' in 1658. The Brömsebro page also moves Bremen and Verden 'from Danish to Swedish control'.

region.text: the ducal (Gottorp) part of Schleswig, 33 cells

ledger.note: 1658: Denmark-Norway recognises the Gottorp dukes' sovereignty over their part of Schleswig. The page says it 'recognized the sovereignty of its dukes over the Gottorp portions of the duchy of Schleswig' under the Treaties of Roskilde (1658) and Copenhagen (1660). Cliopatria draws the land as Holy Roman Empire Minor States from 1662; the duchy of Holstein-Gottorp has no row.

region.text: the Danish island of Zealand

ledger.note: February 1658: Charles X Gustav crosses the frozen belts. Swedish forces 'crossed the frozen straits from Jutland and occupied the Danish island of Zealand', 'with the invasion beginning on 11 February 1658'.

region.text: the Danish island of Zealand

ledger.note: 26 February 1658 (8 March new style): the Treaty of Roskilde ends the Swedish hold on Zealand and leaves Denmark-Norway 'forced to give up a third of its territory to save the rest'.

region.text: the Danish provinces of Scania and Blekinge

ledger.note: 1658: Scania and Blekinge are ceded. 'the ceded lands comprising Blekinge, Bornholm, Bohuslän, Scania and Trøndelag, as well as Halland'; Halland 'was now permanently ceded'. Cliopatria draws the loss in 1659.

union.text: Bohuslän
Nordmøre and Romsdal, then part of Trøndelag

region.text: the Norwegian provinces of Bohuslän and Trøndelag (with Nordmøre and Romsdal)

ledger.note: 1658: the Norwegian provinces of Bohuslän and Trøndelag are ceded. 'This included Norwegian province of Trøndelag and Båhuslen' (Denmark-Norway page); the 46 Møre og Romsdal cells Cliopatria also takes are Nordmøre and Romsdal: the Roskilde page says Trøndelag 'then included Nordmøre and Romsdal' (added by the eu-14-g reviewer).

region.text: the island of Bornholm

ledger.note: 1658: 'The immediate cession of the Danish province of Bornholm to Sweden.'

union.text: the island of Bornholm
Nordmøre and Romsdal, returned with Trøndelag

region.text: Trøndelag and the island of Bornholm

ledger.note: 1660: the Treaty of Copenhagen. 'the resulting Treaty of Copenhagen in 1660 restored Trøndelag to Norway, and the island of Bornholm to Denmark' while 'the other provinces transferred in Roskilde remained Swedish'. Cliopatria draws the return in 1662. Nordmøre and Romsdal, part of Trøndelag in 1658 (Roskilde page), come back with it (added by the eu-14-g reviewer).

region.text: the County of Oldenburg (with Delmenhorst), 15 cells

ledger.note: 1667: the County of Oldenburg comes under the Danish crown. 'Danish kings ruled the county, in a personal union from 1667-1773'; one of five formally separate parts of the union. The region is the 15 cells Cliopatria draws in 1670 (Delmenhorst is not on the page); the county is a member of Cliopatria's Holy Roman Empire Minor States.

region.text: Bremen-Verden (the Prince-Archbishopric of Bremen and Prince-Bishopric of Verden), 27 cells

ledger.note: 1712: Danish troops take Bremen-Verden from Sweden. 'Denmark-Norway occupied plague stricken Bremen-Verden.'

region.text: the ducal (Gottorp) part of Schleswig, 33 cells

ledger.note: 1713: Danish troops hold the Gottorp part of Schleswig. The page says only that 'Danish troops occupied the northern portions of Holstein-Gottorp' during the Great Northern War and gives no year; 1713 is the year of Cliopatria's shape.

region.text: Bremen-Verden (the Prince-Archbishopric of Bremen and Prince-Bishopric of Verden), 27 cells

ledger.note: 1715: Denmark-Norway sells Bremen-Verden. 'Denmark-Norway sold to him [George I] Bremen-Verden, which it kept under occupation since 1712'; Hanover keeps it de facto and Sweden cedes it in the Treaty of Stockholm of 1719. Cliopatria keeps the cells Danish to 1720.

region.text: the ducal (Gottorp) part of Schleswig, 33 cells

ledger.note: 3 July 1720: the Treaty of Frederiksborg ends the Great Northern War for Denmark-Norway; 'Swedish support for Gottorp ceased' (Holstein-Gottorp page).

region.text: the ducal (Gottorp) part of Schleswig, 33 cells

ledger.note: 3 July 1720: 'Denmark also gained full control over Schleswig'; Sweden 'paid 600,000 Riksdaler in damages' and 'Danish-held areas of Swedish Pomerania were returned to Sweden'. The page does not name the Gottorp part; that is the reading from Holstein-Gottorp.

region.text: the County of Oldenburg (with Delmenhorst), 15 cells

ledger.note: 1773: the Treaty of Tsarskoye Selo. The empress 'agreed to cede the territorial claims of her son' to the Gottorp lands still held by Denmark, and in exchange the Gottorp side 'obtained the German countships of Oldenburg and Delmenhorst'; the union of the crowns ran 'from 1667-1773' (Denmark-Norway page).

region.text: the Gottorp lands in Holstein still held by the dukes, 5 cells

ledger.note: 1773: the ducal Holstein lands pass to the Danish crown in the same exchange. The page says the empress 'agreed to cede the territorial claims of her son' to the Gottorp lands still held by Denmark; it does not list Holstein cell by cell.

region.text: 3 cells at Hamburg, Niedersachsen and Syddanmark

ledger.note: 1807: Cliopatria draws 3 cells (Hamburg, Niedersachsen, Syddanmark) as French. Page silent; unverified: page budget.

region.text: 1 Finnmark cell

ledger.note: 1809: Cliopatria hands one Finnmark cell to the Russian Empire. Page silent; unverified: page budget.

region.text: the Kingdom of Norway, renounced 'irrevocably and forever'

ledger.note: 14 January 1814: Norway passes to the King of Sweden. Denmark 'irrevocably and forever' renounced claims to the Kingdom of Norway (Article IV); Greenland, Iceland and the Faroe Islands were 'Excepted' and stayed under the Danish crown. The Norwegians declared independence on 17 May 1814 (Denmark-Norway page).

region.text: the whole realm: Norway to Sweden, Denmark with Schleswig, Holstein, Iceland and the Faroes to the Danish kingdom

ledger.note: 14 January 1814: Denmark-Norway ends at the Treaty of Kiel. 'Denmark-Norway was defeated and King Frederick VI had to cede the Kingdom of Norway' (Denmark-Norway page). The Danish kingdom carries on in kingdom-of-denmark-1814-1940.

wars.note: The page: the war began with the Bornholm clash in May 1563 and the declaration of 13 August 1563.

certainty.note: The Norway-Sweden marches (Jämtland, Härjedalen, Lapland, Finnmark) and the Livonian holdings are approximate; the Sound and the Danish-German frontier on the Eider are not.

Province-by-province treaty cessions in 1645, 1658, 1660, 1720 and 1773 fix the lines; exceptions: Idre and Särna were 'not formally recognised until 1751', and the Arctic frontier in Finnmark stays soft.

notes: Written by the Phase B agent for batch eu-14-g, 2026-10-25. SPLIT: Cliopatria's single 'Denmark-Norway' row (1526-1940, 30 shapes) is Denmark-Norway until the Treaty of Kiel and the Danish kingdom afterwards; this dossier reviews the 22 shapes 1526-1809 and ends in January 1814, the 8 shapes 1814-1940 are in kingdom-of-denmark-1814-1940 (new slug, same batch), so each dossier shows 'no verdict' warnings for the other's shapes. START: the page dates the dual monarchy 1537-1814 but Cliopatria starts 1526, the year after its Kalmar Union row ends; the dossier starts 1526 (confidence 1) to avoid an eleven-year hole, with the page's 1537 as a rename event. WIKIDATA: Q62651 is shared with norway-denmark (1046-1055, one shape); the page dates this union 1537-1814, so that row is a different state (Magnus the Good's union of the 11th century) and is not merged. GREENLAND: the page lists Greenland (2,166,086 km2 in 1800) as a Norwegian overseas possession; it is in none of this row's shapes and no dated event is on the pages, so it is undrawn here; Cliopatria draws the colony as a separate row, Greenland (1734-1940, 24 shapes, 102,479 km2 in 1788-1804), whose dossier should name the Danish-Norwegian crown (reviewer eu-14-g). The Danish colonies (Gold Coast, India, West Indies) have their own rows. COUNTERPARTS: Sweden is kingdom-of-sweden to 1611 and swedish-empire from 1612 in Cliopatria; pairs that straddle 1611 use swedish-empire. The Gottorp and Oldenburg lands use holy-roman-empire-minor-states, the row that carries those cells in Cliopatria (eu-09-c doubts that for Schleswig); the duchy of Holstein-Gottorp deserves its own dossier. UNVERIFIED (page budget; ledger confidence 1): East Finnmark 1595 (24 cells), the 4-cell swaps of 1612 and 1619, the lower Elbe cells of 1622, the 3 cells of 1807 and 1 of 1809, the 1572 loss of Wiek and Pilten, the 1713 date of the ducal Schleswig, Møre og Romsdal (46 cells), Kronoberg (8) and Västerbotten (10) cells leaving in 1645-1658. NOT DRAWN: Danish-held Swedish Pomerania (returned 1720, page gives no dates), Bremen-Verden under Danish administrators 1635-1645, the Scanian War, the Gunboat War. Idre and Särna are a 25 km circle (the gazetteer lacks the name). GAZETTEER: Bornholm, Bohuslän, Idre-Särna, Älvsborg, Bremen-Verden, Halberstadt and Pilten are not names in the gazetteer; Bornholm and Idre-Särna are written as coordinate circles and Bohuslän, Bremen-Verden, Oldenburg and the Gottorp lands as differences of Cliopatria shapes. PAGES: 12 opened for the 22 shapes against a budget of 9 (the Treaty of Kiel and the monarch list are shared with the second dossier; the Lübeck page needed four failed URLs). CALENDAR: Roskilde is dated 26 February 1658 (8 March new style) on the pages; month 2 is used throughout.
